body.objective: Add a fail-closed, content-addressed provenance-relock planner and transaction runner. The first consumer is sf:program/work/bridge-finite-harmonic-tier3-provenance-relock: one backward-compatible Lee-Wald component API change caused a multi-layer stale-hash cascade, and the resident Bridge team currently has to regenerate dozens of producer families in a shared dirty worktree before discovering the next stale frontier. Certlab detects drift well but does not yet compute and execute the minimal topologically ordered relock closure as one auditable migration.
body.stop_condition: Given a target certificate, paper gate or result set and a pinned input commit, compute the exact stale transitive closure from declared dependency_refs plus corroborating code-read edges; classify each edge as producer replay, independent verification, schema migration, paper citation or unresolved/undeclared dependency; emit a deterministic topological batch plan with estimated cache hits and resource hints; execute each batch in an isolated worktree or equivalent candidate tree; run producer and independent verifier rails separately; stop at the first semantic defect; and commit only a complete verified batch. Emit one migration receipt containing old/new hashes, commands, elapsed/resource data, cache keys, changed paths, unresolved drift, and proof that unrelated files were not mutated. Demonstrate the gate on the current Bridge finite-harmonic Tier-3 cascade and either relock it completely or return the exact minimal unresolved semantic frontier.
body.forbid: no blind mass rewriting of hashes; no producer replay counted as independent verification; no mutation in the resident shared worktree; no broad git add; no partial downstream relock committed as if the target gate passed; no traversal based only on filename similarity; no undeclared code-read edge silently promoted to an authoritative dependency; no timeout or skipped verifier treated as pass; no paper theorem promotion by this tool
notes: The current Bridge run is an ideal acceptance fixture because the scoped theorem passes while the package-wide provenance closure is stale.
This should reuse Certlab, the evidence graph, staged-tree verification and content-addressed caches rather than create a separate migration system.
A dry-run plan is useful immediately even before transactional execution lands.
